newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco may delay privatisation of Samir.
newsitem.headline: Morocco may delay privatisation of Samir.

text.p: Morocco may delay the second part of its privatisation of Samir oil refinery due to a lack of interesting offers, officials said on Thursday.
"Samir privatisation is a big business. Investors need enough time to study the project," Abderrafi Menjour, Samir's managing director, was quoted by the authoritative weekly L'Economiste as saying.
It was earlier expected to be offered between November and December this year.
An official at the privatisation ministry said the initial plan to set up Samir's hard core may take place some time in 1997. He declined to give details.
The second tranche estimated at beteen 35 and 51 percent of the firm's stock is to be sold to private investors, including foreign oil companies, to give the refinery a hard core of investors.
The ministry has said seven groups had expressed interest in the project including Total, Shell, Mobil companies.
Morocco floated a first tranche 30 percent of the refinery on the Casablanca stock exchange in March 1996. The flotation raised a total of 2.66 billion dirhams ($310 million).

Located near Casablanca, the refinery has a capacity of 6.25 million tonnes of crude oil a year and satisfies 75 percent of the country's demand for petroleum products. It posted a net profit of 423.3 million dirhams in 1995, up by 130 percent from 1994.
One of the market's 46 listed stocks, Samir was last traded at 250 dirhams per share.
